source.name: usp_GetTopCustomers
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE   PROCEDURE dbo.usp_GetTopCustomers
    @TopN INT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    SELECT TOP (@TopN)
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        ISNULL(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        DATEDIFF(DAY, MAX(o.OrderDate), GETDATE()) AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.usp_GetTopCustomers(
    p_TopN INT
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    CustomerID INT,
    FullName TEXT,
    OrderCount BIGINT,
    TotalSpent NUMERIC,
    DaysSinceLastOrder INT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        COALESCE(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - MAX(o.OrderDate)))::INT AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC
    LIMIT p_TopN;
END;
$$;
assumptions: The CustomerID column is of type INT in the source table
The TotalAmount column in Orders table is a numeric type (DECIMAL/NUMERIC)
The OrderDate column is a DATE or TIMESTAMP type
Schema 'dbo' exists in PostgreSQL database or will be created
FirstName and LastName are text-compatible types (VARCHAR, CHAR, TEXT)
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't send row counts by default for functions)
The procedure returns a result set, so it's converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE

reviewFlags.reason: DATEDIFF behavior differs between SQL Server and PostgreSQL. SQL Server's DATEDIFF(DAY, ...) counts day boundaries crossed, while PostgreSQL's date subtraction calculates actual elapsed time. This may produce different results around midnight boundaries
Verify that TOP N behavior matches LIMIT N for your use case. Both should work identically for positive integers, but edge cases (NULL, 0, negative) may differ

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server procedure converted to PostgreSQL function because it returns a result set. Calling syntax changes from EXEC/EXECUTE to SELECT * FROM function_name(params)
SQL Server '+' operator converted to PostgreSQL '||' operator. NULL handling is similar in both when CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL is ON (SQL Server default)

DATEDIFF(DAY, date1, date2) converted to EXTRACT(DAY FROM (date2 - date1)). PostgreSQL date subtraction returns an INTERVAL, and EXTRACT gets the day component. Results may differ slightly for dates spanning DST changes or when counting day boundaries vs elapsed time
ISNULL() converted to COALESCE(). Both functions behave identically for two-argument cases
GETDATE() converted to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is transaction-scoped in PostgreSQL (constant within transaction), while GETDATE() in SQL Server returns the current time at each call
